component.name: Postio
component.summary: A dense, keyboard-first inbox for a lot of email

description.p: Postio is a local-first email client for IMAP, Gmail and JMAP accounts, built for someone who gets a lot of mail. Its home is one dense inbox, driven from the keyboard, that shows mail as it arrived: sender, subject and first line, with nothing rewritten.

It does four things to that mail and nothing else. It calls out invitations, direct questions and to-dos. It holds newsletters back into digests on a cadence you choose, summarised on this machine when you bring a local model. It files spam and automated updates away, each with its reason and one key from being restored. And it links mail to your Obsidian vault as tasks and notes.

Mail is stored on your machine in an encrypted store with its own full-text index, searched instantly offline. Every action lands locally first and reaches the server in the background. Nothing leaves this machine that you did not ask for: remote images and read receipts stay off until you allow them, and there is no telemetry.

description.p: Postio 0.6.1 is an alpha. It brings back threads: a conversation's messages can be seen and walked again, on the Mac and on Linux alike, and Filtered's tabs sit where the inbox's strip does.

ul.li: Threads in the list: Right expands a conversation in place to show its messages, and Left folds it again. Its row names who took part ("Lena, Ben, you"), how many messages it holds and how many are new. Filtered and search results expand the same way.

Threads in the message window: the thread bar shows each message as a chip, { and } go to the first and the latest message, g u to the first unread, and a thread opens at its first unread message. alt+t lists the thread's outline, and alt+period opens the thread menu.
A reply that arrives while a thread is open shows up live, and a snoozed thread wakes when someone replies to it.

Archive, snooze, labels and mute act on the whole thread, and the footer says what each key will act on. Read state and markers stay per message, and alt+v and alt+Delete move or delete just the one message.
m mutes a thread, and alt+shift+s splits a message and its replies into a thread of their own, which Postio remembers. Both can be undone.
alt+e replies to the latest message. Forwarding asks what to send: this message (1), the whole thread (2), or its attachments (3).
Search answers in threads and opens a thread at the message that matched.
Mail is grouped by subject only within seven days, so unrelated messages that share a subject no longer join one thread.

Filtered's reason tabs are the same square-cornered chip as Has action, in a row the height of the inbox's strip, and its day headings match the inbox's, so the list no longer jumps when you switch between the two views.

description.p: Postio 0.6.0 is an alpha. It brings spec 010's search to Linux, so search works the same way on both platforms, and it moves Postio onto Rust 1.100 and the newest Pimalaya mail libraries, with the protocol and security fixes they carry.

ul.li: Search on Linux: the dropdown as you type, its suggestions and filter chips, and the results view with Quick Look are now on Linux, with the Mac's keys (Command read as Control).
The results' From, To, Date, Anywhere and Label filters open from the keyboard: alt+f, alt+t, alt+d, alt+w and alt+l, each shown as a keycap on its button and in the View menu.

Search reads more truthfully: a value nobody matches says so instead of showing an empty heading, People leaves you out of its count, a top hit's matches count toward Quick Look, and passages that arrive with the first page are no longer dropped.
A flag change made just before archiving a message now reaches the server, and Filtered's decisions carry to your other machines.
In the reader, Ctrl+C copies what you selected. A move's toast counts the messages you chose.
On the Mac, Shift+Tab steps back through the composer, the message's buttons show hover and press, and the sync label stays inside its capsule.
IMAP, SMTP, OAuth and JMAP move to the latest Pimalaya libraries:
After a MOVE or COPY, each message's new UID is paired with the right original.
A server's QRESYNC answer can no longer make Postio allocate gigabytes.
Passwords are SASLprep-prepared, and a SCRAM server's iteration count is bounded.
A FETCH line that decodes only in part is never stored as a message missing its date or envelope. An incremental resync that lost one rebuilds the folder instead.
Security: the HTML sanitizer is on ammonia 4.2.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0533, mutation XSS through embedded SVG and MathML), and rustix on 1.1.6 (RUSTSEC-2026-0486).
Under the hood: Rust 1.100, html5ever 0.40, zbus 6 with oo7 0.7 for the keyring, and the Flatpak bundles on GNOME 51 and freedesktop 26.08.

description.p: Postio 0.5.0 is an alpha, and the first release with a Mac app to download. It is the release where the one dense inbox, and the four things it does to mail, became the app on both platforms, over one engine.

ul.li: One inbox, on Linux and the Mac: one list of mail as it arrived; invitations, direct questions and to-dos called out on their rows with the sentence that raised them; digests on a cadence you choose; Filtered, with its reason on every row and one key to restore it, and now multi-select there as in any folder.
The native macOS app is released: `postio-0.5.0-macos-arm64.zip`, Apple silicon, macOS 14 or newer. It is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so open it once with right-click → Open.
Search moves with you: a dropdown as you type, facets for sender, date and more, and a results view with Files and People tabs, Quick Look and save.
Contacts, on both platforms: the people in your mail, editable, mergeable, with vCard import and export.
An MCP server lets an agent you connect read the mail you share with it, and archive, move and label it. Settings shows each agent's access and revokes it. Nothing is shared until you share it.
The reader paints a sender's own page on paper, or the message in the app's colours; zoom, find in the message, darken a sheet, and fall back visibly when a render runs past its deadline.
Notifications on the Mac follow `[sync] notify_roles`, as on Linux: mail arriving in Trash, Spam or Archive no longer notifies.

Retrieval is sturdier: a moved message keeps its body and is not shown twice, a header-only refresh keeps the body already fetched, a refused download says so at once, a message open while the connection drops loads as soon as it returns, and an account signed in again asks its new connection for what was waiting.

Under the hood: mail-parser 1.0 (damaged base64 recovered instead of stored as text, RFC 2231 names and encoded words decoded across their pieces, a date's `+5` read as +05:00) and mail-builder 2.0 (control characters can no longer inject a header through an address); Turso 0.8.3 with its full-text index on tantivy 0.27; Rust 1.99.1.

description.p: Postio 0.4.2 is an alpha, and the first release since the local store was rebuilt. The mail client is the same one the maintainer reads mail in every day; what changed underneath is the engine, and what changed on top is a long list of things that used to wait.

ul.li: The store is Turso, a Rust rewrite of SQLite, with its own full-text index and page-level encryption. Your mail is stored the same way; what is gone is the vendored SQLCipher and OpenSSL build underneath it.

Search and navigation stay responsive while a large mailbox backfills: a keystroke takes priority over a sync pass for the store, and the full-text index of message bodies is built by its own task off the sync lane.
Message bodies are compressed per row and stamped with the parser that read them, so a body an older parser got wrong is fetched again on the next sync instead of staying wrong.
Messages whose quoted-printable encoding is not quite right are decoded leniently instead of showing "parts of this message could not be decoded".
Settled operations are pruned from the queue after thirty days and the store reclaims space when it is worth doing.
The macOS frontend over the same engine reads mail, searches and pages, and is built and tested but not yet released.
A WebKit process that dies is reported at once, in the app and in the test suite, instead of surfacing as a four-minute timeout.

A mailto: link from a browser or another application opens the composer with the address, subject and body filled in, including on a cold launch. The desktop entry had claimed the scheme since 0.1.0; the application had never handled it.

The 0.3.0 milestone is included in this release: several accounts with a unified inbox, OAuth 2 sign-in through the browser, and the Gmail and JMAP backends. Its tag was cut on 2026-09-11 but its release never published, so this is the first bundle that carries it.

There is no 0.4.0 or 0.4.1 bundle. Both tags were cut on 2026-09-19 and neither build reached the bundle — the release path had never once run to completion, and each attempt uncovered the next thing wrong with it. Nothing was ever published under either tag; 0.4.2 is the same contents, released.

description.p: The multiple-accounts and OAuth milestone. Its tag was cut on 2026-09-11, but the release workflow failed before publishing anything, so no bundle was ever shipped under this number; 0.4.0 is the first release that carries this work.

ul.li: Several accounts, each synced by its own engine, and a unified inbox that groups threads across accounts at read time.
Moving mail between accounts as a safe saga, and search scoped to one account with account:.
OAuth 2 sign-in through the system browser with PKCE; OAUTHBEARER and XOAUTH2 on IMAP and SMTP; automatic re-authentication when a refresh grant expires.
Gmail REST and JMAP backends behind the same MailBackend seam as IMAP.

description.p: One IMAP + SMTP account, fully usable offline after the first sync: inbox, folders and threads; read, archive, delete, flag and move; HTML and plaintext reading with attachments and quoted-message folding; compose, reply, reply-all, forward and drafts; local full-text search with an instant search box and operators; vim-style keyboard navigation, a command palette and configurable shortcuts; background sync and local undo.
